We know that the line passes through the points $P(-1,3,2)$ and $Q(2,4,5).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1+3t \\ 3+t \\ 2+3t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-1+3t \\ y=3+t \\ z=2+3t\end{aligned}
$$
